extracted_claims.text: Article 43 of the AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) establishes that high-risk AI systems must undergo conformity assessment before being placed on the market, with two possible routes: internal control (Annex VI) or quality management system plus technical documentation assessment by a notified body (Annex VII).

For high-risk AI systems listed in point 1 of Annex III (e.g., biometric identification), the provider may use internal control (Annex VI) if harmonised standards or common specifications were applied and complied with; otherwise Annex VII assessment with a notified body is required.

For high-risk AI systems referred to in points 2 to 8 of Annex III, providers generally follow the internal control procedure under Annex VI (self-assessment using their own quality management system), without mandatory involvement of a notified body.

For high-risk AI systems covered by existing EU product safety legislation listed in Section A of Annex I (e.g., medical devices, machinery), providers must follow the relevant conformity assessment procedures under that sectoral legislation, with notified bodies additionally verifying compliance with the AI-specific requirements of the AI Act.

Providers may choose any notified body for the Annex VII procedure, except where the high-risk AI system is intended to be put into service by law enforcement, immigration or asylum authorities or EU institutions/bodies/agencies, in which case the relevant market surveillance authority under Article 74(8) or (9) acts as the notified body.

A new conformity assessment is required if a high-risk AI system is substantially modified, except for predetermined changes in systems that continue to learn after being placed on the market or put into service.

Article 46 allows a market surveillance authority to authorise, by derogation from Article 43 and upon a duly justified request, the placing on the market or putting into service of specific high-risk AI systems for a limited period, for exceptional reasons of public security, protection of life and health, environmental protection, or protection of key industrial and infrastructural assets.

Annex VII allows a notified body, where necessary and after other reasonable means to verify conformity have been exhausted, to request access (upon reasoned request) to the training and trained models of the AI system, including relevant parameters, subject to existing EU law on intellectual property and trade secrets.
Article 35 of the AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) establishes the administrative framework for identification numbers and lists of notified bodies.

As of March 2026, the notified body ecosystem for the AI Act was still being built, with designation processes ongoing across Member States, limited capacity, and uncertain timelines, despite an August 2026 deadline for high-risk obligations.
As of April 2026, no notified bodies had been formally designated under the AI Act.

High-risk AI obligations under the AI Act are stated to fully apply from August 2026 (with some sources citing August 2, 2026 and others August 2026 generally), after which notified bodies designated under the AI Act would begin conducting AI Act-specific conformity assessments.

A Council document (ST-7322-2026-INIT) references codes and categories (e.g., AIP 0101–0105) used to set the scope of designation of conformity assessment bodies notified under Article 30 of the referenced Regulation, corresponding to AI systems subject to Annex I of the AI Act.

A Commission proposal (COM(2025) 836 / 2025/0359 (COD)) proposes creating a new Annex XIV listing codes and categories of AI systems for the Commission's NANDO information system, and amending Regulation (EU) 2018/1139 to integrate AI Act high-risk requirements into aviation safety regulation.

As of October 2025, the NANDO system listed 51 MDR-designated notified bodies and 19 IVDR-designated notified bodies, but these figures pertain to the Medical Devices Regulation and In Vitro Diagnostic Regulation, not the AI Act specifically.

Under the Cyber Resilience Act (a separate but related EU regulation), as of late June 2026 zero notified bodies had been designated in the Commission's NANDO database, with a target of 11 December 2026 for sufficient notified body capacity and full application from 11 December 2027.

The 2021 proposal version of Article 43 (25 November 2022 text) required providers of Annex III point 1 high-risk AI systems to follow one of the listed conformity assessment procedures when applying harmonised standards or common specifications referenced in Articles 40-41.

The Commission has the power under Article 43(5) to adopt delegated acts (per Article 97) to update Annex VI and Annex VII conformity assessment procedures in light of technical progress, without needing to revise the AI Act itself.

report:
# Conformity Assessment Procedures for High-Risk AI Systems Under the EU AI Act and the Status of Notified Body Designation

## Executive Summary
The EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) establishes a dual-track conformity assessment system for high-risk AI systems under Article 43, combining internal control (self-assessment) with third-party notified body review for certain categories, most notably standalone biometric identification systems ([Article 43](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43), high confidence). However, as of the most recent available reporting (March–April 2026), no notified bodies appear to have been formally designated under the AI Act itself, creating significant uncertainty about readiness ahead of the August 2026 deadline for high-risk obligations ([eyreact.com](https://eyreact.com/notified-bodies-ai-act); [aiact-navigator.com](https://aiact-navigator.com/blog/eu-ai-act-medical-devices-mdr-ivdr-interplay-guide), low confidence).

## Key Findings

### Conformity Assessment Procedures
Article 43 provides that high-risk AI systems must undergo conformity assessment before being placed on the market, via either internal control under Annex VI or a quality management system plus technical documentation assessment by a notified body under Annex VII (high confidence) ([Article 43](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43)). For Annex III point 1 systems (e.g., biometric identification), providers may use the internal control route only if harmonised standards or common specifications were applied and complied with; otherwise Annex VII assessment involving a notified body is mandatory (low confidence) ([futurium.ec.europa.eu](https://futurium.ec.europa.eu/sites/default/files/2021-10/Kop_EU%20Artificial%20Intelligence%20Act%20-%20The%20European%20Approach%20to%20AI_21092021_0.pdf)). For the remaining Annex III categories (points 2–8), providers generally follow the Annex VI internal control procedure without mandatory notified body involvement (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/ga/ai-act/article-43)). Where high-risk AI systems are already covered by sectoral EU product safety legislation (Annex I, Section A—e.g., medical devices, machinery), providers follow that legislation's existing conformity assessment procedures, with notified bodies additionally verifying AI-specific requirements (medium-high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43); [VDE](https://www.vde.com/topics-en/artificial-intelligence/blog/conformity-assessment-high-risk-ai)).

Providers may generally choose any notified body for Annex VII assessments, except where systems are intended for use by law enforcement, immigration, asylum authorities, or EU institutions, in which case the relevant market surveillance authority acts as the notified body under Article 74(8)/(9) (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/ga/ai-act/article-43)). A new conformity assessment is required following substantial modification of a system, with exceptions for predetermined changes in continuously learning systems (medium confidence) ([Article 43](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43)). Article 46 permits market surveillance authorities to derogate from Article 43 and authorise market placement for limited periods on exceptional public security, health, environmental, or infrastructure grounds (medium confidence) ([Article 46](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-46)). Annex VII also grants notified bodies the right to request access to training and trained models, including parameters, when other verification means are exhausted, subject to IP and trade secret protections (medium confidence) ([Annex VII](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/annex-7)).

### Designation Framework and Status
Article 35 establishes the administrative framework for identification numbers and lists of notified bodies (low confidence) ([regulation-ai.eu](https://www.regulation-ai.eu/en/articles/article-35)). A Council document (ST-7322-2026-INIT) references coding categories (AIP 0101–0105) used to scope designation of conformity assessment bodies under Article 30, tied to Annex I systems (medium confidence) ([Council document](https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-7322-2026-INIT/en/pdf)). A separate Commission proposal (COM(2025) 836) would create a new Annex XIV listing AI system codes for the NANDO database and amend aviation safety Regulation 2018/1139 to integrate AI Act requirements (medium confidence) ([Council document](https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-15708-2025-INIT/en/pdf)); its adoption status is unclear.

As of March–April 2026, sources indicate the notified body ecosystem for the AI Act was still being built, with designation processes ongoing but no bodies formally designated (low confidence) ([eyreact.com](https://eyreact.com/notified-bodies-ai-act); [aiact-navigator.com](https://aiact-navigator.com/blog/eu-ai-act-medical-devices-mdr-ivdr-interplay-guide)). By comparison, as of October 2025 NANDO listed 51 MDR and 19 IVDR notified bodies, but these pertain to medical devices regulation, not the AI Act (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A52025SC1051)). A similar designation lag was reported under the related Cyber Resilience Act, with zero notified bodies designated as of late June 2026 (low confidence) ([cybercertlabs.com](https://www.cybercertlabs.com/case-studies/insights-cra-notified-bodies-2026)).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
Sources differ in characterizing designation progress: one describes "ongoing processes" (low confidence, March 2026) while another states flatly "zero designations" (low confidence, April 2026); it is unclear whether these reflect genuine differences in timing or differing standards of what counts as "progress." Both claims carry low confidence (0.12–0.14) and should be treated cautiously. The 2022 proposal text of Article 43 (low confidence, 0.20–0.24) reflects a pre-final draft and may not match the adopted regulation's final wording.

## Knowledge Gaps
No source identifies any specific notified body formally designated under the AI Act. The expected number of notified bodies, lead Member States, and current (post-April 2026) status remain unreported. The precise Annex III categories requiring mandatory notified body involvement beyond biometrics (point 1) versus internal control (points 2–8) are not fully detailed. The interaction between COM(2025) 836's proposed Annex XIV and the existing Article 43/Annex VI/VII framework, and its legislative status, is unclear. The relationship between AI Act notified body designation and existing MDR/IVDR notified bodies for medical AI systems is not clarified.

# Conformity Assessment Procedures for High-Risk AI Systems Under the EU AI Act and the Status of Notified Body Designation

## Executive Summary
The EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) establishes a dual-track conformity assessment system for high-risk AI systems under Article 43, combining internal control (self-assessment) with third-party notified body review for certain categories, most notably standalone biometric identification systems ([Article 43](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43), high confidence). However, as of the most recent available reporting (March–April 2026), no notified bodies appear to have been formally designated under the AI Act itself, creating significant uncertainty about readiness ahead of the August 2026 deadline for high-risk obligations ([eyreact.com](https://eyreact.com/notified-bodies-ai-act); [aiact-navigator.com](https://aiact-navigator.com/blog/eu-ai-act-medical-devices-mdr-ivdr-interplay-guide), low confidence).

## Key Findings

### Conformity Assessment Procedures
Article 43 provides that high-risk AI systems must undergo conformity assessment before being placed on the market, via either internal control under Annex VI or a quality management system plus technical documentation assessment by a notified body under Annex VII (high confidence) ([Article 43](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43)). For Annex III point 1 systems (e.g., biometric identification), providers may use the internal control route only if harmonised standards or common specifications were applied and complied with; otherwise Annex VII assessment involving a notified body is mandatory (low confidence) ([futurium.ec.europa.eu](https://futurium.ec.europa.eu/sites/default/files/2021-10/Kop_EU%20Artificial%20Intelligence%20Act%20-%20The%20European%20Approach%20to%20AI_21092021_0.pdf)). For the remaining Annex III categories (points 2–8), providers generally follow the Annex VI internal control procedure without mandatory notified body involvement (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/ga/ai-act/article-43)). Where high-risk AI systems are already covered by sectoral EU product safety legislation (Annex I, Section A—e.g., medical devices, machinery), providers follow that legislation's existing conformity assessment procedures, with notified bodies additionally verifying AI-specific requirements (medium-high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43); [VDE](https://www.vde.com/topics-en/artificial-intelligence/blog/conformity-assessment-high-risk-ai)).

Providers may generally choose any notified body for Annex VII assessments, except where systems are intended for use by law enforcement, immigration, asylum authorities, or EU institutions, in which case the relevant market surveillance authority acts as the notified body under Article 74(8)/(9) (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/ga/ai-act/article-43)). A new conformity assessment is required following substantial modification of a system, with exceptions for predetermined changes in continuously learning systems (medium confidence) ([Article 43](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43)). Article 46 permits market surveillance authorities to derogate from Article 43 and authorise market placement for limited periods on exceptional public security, health, environmental, or infrastructure grounds (medium confidence) ([Article 46](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-46)). Annex VII also grants notified bodies the right to request access to training and trained models, including parameters, when other verification means are exhausted, subject to IP and trade secret protections (medium confidence) ([Annex VII](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/annex-7)).

### Designation Framework and Status
Article 35 establishes the administrative framework for identification numbers and lists of notified bodies (low confidence) ([regulation-ai.eu](https://www.regulation-ai.eu/en/articles/article-35)). A Council document (ST-7322-2026-INIT) references coding categories (AIP 0101–0105) used to scope designation of conformity assessment bodies under Article 30, tied to Annex I systems (medium confidence) ([Council document](https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-7322-2026-INIT/en/pdf)). A separate Commission proposal (COM(2025) 836) would create a new Annex XIV listing AI system codes for the NANDO database and amend aviation safety Regulation 2018/1139 to integrate AI Act requirements (medium confidence) ([Council document](https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-15708-2025-INIT/en/pdf)); its adoption status is unclear.

As of March–April 2026, sources indicate the notified body ecosystem for the AI Act was still being built, with designation processes ongoing but no bodies formally designated (low confidence) ([eyreact.com](https://eyreact.com/notified-bodies-ai-act); [aiact-navigator.com](https://aiact-navigator.com/blog/eu-ai-act-medical-devices-mdr-ivdr-interplay-guide)). By comparison, as of October 2025 NANDO listed 51 MDR and 19 IVDR notified bodies, but these pertain to medical devices regulation, not the AI Act (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A52025SC1051)). A similar designation lag was reported under the related Cyber Resilience Act, with zero notified bodies designated as of late June 2026 (low confidence) ([cybercertlabs.com](https://www.cybercertlabs.com/case-studies/insights-cra-notified-bodies-2026)).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
Sources differ in characterizing designation progress: one describes "ongoing processes" (low confidence, March 2026) while another states flatly "zero designations" (low confidence, April 2026); it is unclear whether these reflect genuine differences in timing or differing standards of what counts as "progress." Both claims carry low confidence (0.12–0.14) and should be treated cautiously. The 2022 proposal text of Article 43 (low confidence, 0.20–0.24) reflects a pre-final draft and may not match the adopted regulation's final wording.

## Knowledge Gaps
No source identifies any specific notified body formally designated under the AI Act. The expected number of notified bodies, lead Member States, and current (post-April 2026) status remain unreported. The precise Annex III categories requiring mandatory notified body involvement beyond biometrics (point 1) versus internal control (points 2–8) are not fully detailed. The interaction between COM(2025) 836's proposed Annex XIV and the existing Article 43/Annex VI/VII framework, and its legislative status, is unclear. The relationship between AI Act notified body designation and existing MDR/IVDR notified bodies for medical AI systems is not clarified.
